newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-YORKE ENDS GOAL FAMINE WITH HAT-TRICK BUT VILLA LOSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YORKE ENDS GOAL FAMINE WITH HAT-TRICK BUT VILLA LOSE.

text.p: Dwight Yorke ended his goal famine this season with a hat-trick against Newcastle on Monday but it was not enough to save 10-man Aston Villa from a 4-3 premier league defeat.
Yorke, scorer of 25 goals last season, netted his first of this campaign just four minutes into Monday's thrilling match at St James's Park.

Newcastle were level through Les Ferdinand within 90 seconds and by half-time Villa, seeking a lift after last week's UEFA Cup elimination by Swedish club Helsingborgs, were 3-1 behind, down to 10 men and seemingly out of it.
They had Mark Draper sent off in the 43rd minute for a second bookable offence.
But if Newcastle, pipped for the league title by Manchester United last season, were expecting an easy ride in the second half, they were in for a shock.

Yorke, a constant threat to the Newcastle defence, scored a superb solo goal in the 59th minute to cut the deficit to 3-2 and after Steve Howey had headed the home side into a 4-2 lead in the 67th minute, Yorke popped up two minutes later to complete his hat-trick.
He had the ball in the net again a few minutes later but Newcastle fans breathed a sigh of relief when it was ruled offside.
Ferdinand also came close to a hat-trick in a match of seesawing fortunes.
After netting his first from close range from Alan Shearer's cross, he headed his second -- his eighth of the season -- from Keith Gillespie's cross in the 22nd minute.
A goal-line clearance by Ugo Ehiogu prevented Ferdinand from completing a hat-trick in the 38th minute. But Ehiogu's valiant defending was all in vain as Shearer followed up to score.
Newcastle's hard-fought win lifted them to second place in the premier league, two points behind Liverpool.
